title: Phish brought near-record crowds to this Fenway dispensary — but not a product shortage
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Phish fans matched New Dia Fenway's record sales during concerts, with no product shortages reported.
New Dia Fenway hosted Phish Phan Art event benefiting the Mockingbird Foundation during the weekend.
The dispensary prepared for high demand by planning inventory for major event weekends in Fenway.

title: Red Sox homer 3 times over 7 pitches en route to statement sweep of Dodgers
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Red Sox achieved an 8-4 win over the Dodgers, completing a three-game sweep in Los Angeles.
Ceddanne Rafaela, Wilyer Abreu, and Masataka Yoshida hit three home runs over seven pitches in the third inning.
Boston holds the second AL Wild Card spot after winning 23 of their last 27 games, with a 60-51 record.

title: Rafaela homers for 3rd straight game as the Red Sox beat the Dodgers 8-4 for 3-game sweep
author: The Associated Press
bullets: Ceddanne Rafaela hit a home run for the third game in a row as the Red Sox swept the Dodgers.
Jake Bennett allowed three runs over 5 2/3 innings, improving his record to 7-4 for the season.
Masataka Yoshida contributed a homer and two RBIs in the Red Sox's 8-4 victory over the Dodgers.

title: Stoughton police chief and town manager placed on leave amid investigation after chief alleges discrimination, harrassment
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Stoughton Police Chief Donna McNamara and Town Manager Thomas Calter placed on paid leave amid discrimination and harassment allegations.
McNamara's lawsuit claims Calter harassed her due to gender and pressured her resignation; Calter denies allegations.
Separate investigations launched, with Marc Tisdelle acting as town manager; no response yet from Calter or town to the lawsuit.

title: Here’s what meteorologists are saying about heavy rain and possible flooding Monday
author: Jack Pickell
bullets: National Weather Service warns of localized flooding risk due to thunderstorms and heavy rain overnight into Monday.
Urban areas with poor drainage face greatest flood risk, particularly in interior Massachusetts, northwest Rhode Island, and Connecticut.
Meteorologists cite extreme atmospheric moisture and a cold front as factors increasing flood and severe weather risks Monday.

title: Review & setlist: Phish soars over Fenway for two nights of rarities and redefined favorites
author: Perry Eaton
bullets: Phish performed two concerts at Fenway Park, featuring rare songs and unexpected surprises for fans.
The band played a 20-minute version of 'What's Going Through Your Mind' and covered XTC's 'Melt The Guns'.
Phish's setlists included their classics like 'Harry Hood' and 'Tweezer', while showcasing new material.

title: Former Patriots 2024 2nd-round pick abruptly retires from NFL
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Ja'Lynn Polk, former Patriots 2024 second-round pick, retires at 24 after being placed on reserve/retired list by the Saints.
Polk played one season for the Patriots, recording 12 catches for 87 yards and two touchdowns in 2024.
After being traded to the Saints, Polk was sidelined by injuries and did not play in the 2025 season.

title: Mother of trooper killed in crash sues Saugus restaurant, alleging it over-served wrong-way driver
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Trooper Kevin Trainor's mother sues a Saugus restaurant, alleging it over-served driver Hernan Marrero causing a fatal crash.
Hernan Marrero consumed at least nine drinks at Tribu Mexican Kitchen & Bar before the crash, with a blood alcohol level of 0.192.
The lawsuit claims restaurant staff failed to prevent Marrero from driving despite knowing he was visibly intoxicated and impaired.

title: Red Sox trade deadline live updates: Will Craig Breslow make another big move?
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Red Sox Chief Baseball Officer Craig Breslow seeks another major move before MLB's trade deadline on Monday at 6 p.m.
Boston acquired infielder Curtis Mead from the Nationals, but Mead's debut injury has left the team needing more reinforcements.
The Red Sox are reportedly interested in players like CJ Abrams and Zach Neto, though trades could demand significant prospects.

title: Man killed in East Boston overnight shooting
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: A man was fatally shot near 464 Meridian St. in East Boston early Sunday morning.
The victim was pronounced dead at a local hospital; his identity awaits autopsy and family notification.
No arrests have been made; BPD Homicide Unit asks for information at 617-343-4470.
